info.title: Ambivo Custom Objects API
info.description:
Custom Objects and Custom Modules (Legacy) for the Ambivo platform.

## Custom Objects

Custom Objects are user-defined entities stored in a dedicated custom database (`ambivo_customdb`).
Each object gets its own MongoDB collection named `amb_<tenant_id>_<collection_id>` with a
JSON Schema validator.

Metadata is stored in `collection_metadata` (custom DB). Access is controlled in two layers.

**Layer 1, the collection gate.** Checked before any `/custom/object/data` call.
- `object_access_dict`: who can see the definition (`R`). Only a tenant admin can create, change or delete a definition.
- `data_access_dict`: which letters (`C`, `R`, `U`, `D`) each user has on the object's records.
  Keys are a userid, `*` (everyone in the tenant) or `all` (value `"*"`).
  The default is `{<creator>: [C,R,U,D], "*": ["C"]}`. With that default, other users can create records
  and get HTTP 403 on every read, update and delete. Set `"*": ["C","R","U","D"]` for a shared app.

**Layer 2, the record.** Checked on every read and write of a record.
- A user may act on a record they own (`userid`), or one whose `access_dict` grants them the letter.
- `access_dict` keys: a userid, `*` or `all`. `{"*": ["R"]}` lets everyone in the tenant read the record.
- `default_access_dict` on the object is copied to each new record's `access_dict`. Without it a new
  record has `{}`, so only its owner and tenant admins see it.
- Guests never get the `*` or `all` grants. They reach a record only by owning it or by their own userid key.
- Tenant admins skip both layers.

## Custom Modules (Legacy)

Legacy module-based custom collections. **Planned for deprecation** — use Custom Objects
(`/custom/object`) instead.

Modules group multiple collections under a single container with inherited access control.
Stored in `custom_modules` collection in the main database.

## Database Architecture

| Database | Collection | Purpose |
|----------|-----------|---------|
| `ambivo` (main) | `custom_modules` | Legacy module definitions |
| `ambivo_customdb` | `collection_metadata` | Custom Object definitions |
| `ambivo_customdb` | `amb_<tenant_id>_<collection_id>` | Actual data collections |

## Tenant Cleanup

When a tenant is deleted, all `collection_metadata` records for that tenant are removed
and all `amb_<tenant_id>_*` collections are dropped from the custom database.

## Reference Fields (Cross-Collection References)

Custom objects support cross-collection references via `reference_fields` on the object
definition. This provides **master-child relationships** and **foreign-key-style validation**
without MongoDB-level constraints — all enforcement is **application-level and fail-safe**.

### How It Works

1. **Define** — add `reference_fields` when creating or updating the object definition (`POST /custom/object` or `PUT /custom/object`)
2. **Validate** — on record create/update, the API checks that referenced records exist in the target collection
3. **Enforce** — on record delete, on-delete policies (`restrict`, `nullify`, `cascade`, `none`) are applied

Reference field values are stored as **plain strings** (the `_id` of the referenced record).
The `reference_fields` metadata tells the API how to validate and handle deletions.

### On-Delete Policies

| Policy | Behavior | Use Case |
|--------|----------|----------|
| `none` | No action — orphan children allowed | Loose coupling, audit trails |
| `restrict` | Block parent delete if children exist | Prevent data loss, strong integrity |
| `nullify` | Remove the reference field from the child on parent delete | Soft unlinking |
| `cascade` | Delete child records when parent is deleted | Tightly coupled children (order items, invoice lines) |

### Multi-Level Cascade Example

```
orders (parent)
  └── order_items (child, order_id → orders._id, on_delete: cascade)
        └── item_notes (grandchild, item_id → order_items._id, on_delete: cascade)
```

When an order is deleted:
1. `order_items` with matching `order_id` are cascade-deleted.
2. The cascade goes one level only. The deleted `order_items` do not run their own policies.
3. `item_notes` that pointed at those items stay, with an `item_id` that points at nothing.
   To clear them, delete the items first with `action=delete_many`, then delete the order.

### End-to-End cURL Walkthrough

**Step 1 — Create parent object (orders):**
```bash
curl -X POST https://ingress.ambivo.com/custom/object \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "collection_id": "orders",
    "name": "Orders",
    "schema": {
      "order_number": {"bsonType": "string"},
      "customer_name": {"bsonType": "string"},
      "total_amount": {"bsonType": "double"}
    },
    "required_fields": ["order_number"],
    "indexes": [{"fields": ["order_number"], "unique": true}]
  }'
```

**Step 2 — Create child object (order_items) with reference_fields:**
```bash
curl -X POST https://ingress.ambivo.com/custom/object \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "collection_id": "order_items",
    "name": "Order Items",
    "schema": {
      "order_id": {"bsonType": "string", "description": "FK to orders"},
      "product_name": {"bsonType": "string"},
      "quantity": {"bsonType": "int"},
      "unit_price": {"bsonType": "double"}
    },
    "required_fields": ["order_id", "product_name"],
    "reference_fields": {
      "order_id": {
        "target_collection": "orders",
        "target_field": "_id",
        "on_delete": "cascade",
        "validate": true,
        "display_field": "order_number"
      }
    },
    "indexes": [{"fields": ["order_id"]}]
  }'
```

**Step 3 — Create grandchild object (item_notes) with reference_fields:**
```bash
curl -X POST https://ingress.ambivo.com/custom/object \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "collection_id": "item_notes",
    "name": "Item Notes",
    "schema": {
      "item_id": {"bsonType": "string", "description": "FK to order_items"},
      "note_text": {"bsonType": "string"}
    },
    "required_fields": ["item_id", "note_text"],
    "reference_fields": {
      "item_id": {
        "target_collection": "order_items",
        "target_field": "_id",
        "on_delete": "cascade",
        "validate": true,
        "display_field": "product_name"
      }
    },
    "indexes": [{"fields": ["item_id"]}]
  }'
```

**Step 4 — Create a parent record:**
```bash
curl -X POST https://ingress.ambivo.com/custom/object/data \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "collection_id": "orders",
    "data": {"order_number": "ORD-001", "customer_name": "Acme Corp", "total_amount": 500.00}
  }'
# Response: {"result": 1, "id": "ORDER_ID_HERE", ...}
```

**Step 5 — Create a child record (validated):**
```bash
curl -X POST https://ingress.ambivo.com/custom/object/data \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "collection_id": "order_items",
    "data": {"order_id": "ORDER_ID_HERE", "product_name": "Widget A", "quantity": 10, "unit_price": 25.00}
  }'
# API validates that ORDER_ID_HERE exists in the orders collection
# If not found → {"result": 2, "error_code": "REFERENCE_VALIDATION_FAILED", ...}
```

**Step 6 — Create a grandchild record:**
```bash
curl -X POST https://ingress.ambivo.com/custom/object/data \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "collection_id": "item_notes",
    "data": {"item_id": "ITEM_ID_HERE", "note_text": "Shipped via UPS"}
  }'
```

**Step 7 — Delete the parent. Its direct children are deleted:**
```bash
curl -X DELETE "https://ingress.ambivo.com/custom/object/data?collection_id=orders&id=ORDER_ID_HERE" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# Response:
# {
#   "result": 1,
#   "deleted_count": 1,
#   "reference_cleanup": {
#     "checked": 1,          ← reference fields that point at orders
#     "restricted": [],
#     "nullified": 0,
#     "cascaded": 2          ← order_items deleted; their item_notes stay
#   }
# }
# reference_cleanup is present only when something was nullified or cascaded.
```

**Step 8 — Attempting to create a child with invalid reference:**
```bash
curl -X POST https://ingress.ambivo.com/custom/object/data \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "collection_id": "order_items",
    "data": {"order_id": "nonexistent_id_123", "product_name": "Widget B", "quantity": 1, "unit_price": 10.00}
  }'
# Response:
# {
#   "result": 2,
#   "error_code": "REFERENCE_VALIDATION_FAILED",
#   "reference_errors": [{
#     "field": "order_id",
#     "value": "nonexistent_id_123",
#     "target_collection": "orders",
#     "error": "REFERENCED_RECORD_NOT_FOUND"
#   }]
# }
```

**Step 9 — Change on_delete policy (e.g. from cascade to restrict):**
```bash
curl -X PUT https://ingress.ambivo.com/custom/object \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "collection_id": "order_items",
    "reference_fields": {
      "order_id": {
        "target_collection": "orders",
        "target_field": "_id",
        "on_delete": "restrict",
        "validate": true,
        "display_field": "order_number"
      }
    }
  }'
```

Now deleting an order that has items returns:
```json
{
  "result": 2,
  "error_code": "DELETE_RESTRICTED",
  "error": {
    "message": "Cannot delete: 2 record(s) in 'order_items' reference this record via 'order_id'. Delete or unlink the child records first.",
    "referencing_collection": "order_items",
    "referencing_field": "order_id",
    "child_count": 2
  }
}
```

### Data Flow Diagram

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                 REFERENCE FIELDS DATA FLOW                       │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                   │
│  DEFINE (POST/PUT /custom/object)                                │
│  ─────────────────────────────────                               │
│  reference_fields stored in collection_metadata                  │
│  e.g. {"order_id": {"target_collection": "orders", ...}}        │
│                                                                   │
│  CREATE / UPDATE (POST/PUT /custom/object/data)                  │
│  ──────────────────────────────────────────────                  │
│  1. Load reference_fields from collection_metadata               │
│  2. For each ref field present in the data payload:              │
│     ├─ Skip if value is null/empty or validate=false             │
│     ├─ Query target_collection for matching record               │
│     ├─ If not found or not an id → REFERENCE_VALIDATION_FAILED   │
│     └─ If DB error → log warning, allow (fail-safe)              │
│                                                                   │
│  DELETE (DELETE /custom/object/data)                              │
│  ──────────────────────────────────                              │
│  1. PRE-CHECK: Find all collections whose reference_fields       │
│     point to this collection                                     │
│     ├─ If on_delete="restrict" and children exist → BLOCK        │
│     └─ Otherwise proceed                                         │
│  2. EXECUTE: Delete the record                                   │
│  3. POST-CLEANUP: For each referencing collection:               │
│     ├─ on_delete="none"    → skip (orphans allowed)              │
│     ├─ on_delete="nullify" → $unset {ref_field}                  │
│     └─ on_delete="cascade" → delete_many on the children.        │
│        One level only: the children's own policies do not run.  │
│                                                                   │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │  WHY NOT MongoDB TRIGGERS?                                 │  │
│  │                                                            │  │
│  │  • Fail-safe — app code catches errors, never crashes      │  │
│  │  • Visible — cleanup reported in API response              │  │
│  │  • Controllable — change policy via PUT, no restart        │  │
│  │  • Simple — no Change Stream cursor, no background worker  │  │
│  │  • Tenant-isolated — per-collection metadata, not global   │  │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                                                                   │
│  IMPORTANT NOTES:                                                │
│  • delete_all applies on-delete policies; skips workflows, rules  │
│  • Cascade deletes skip workflows and automation rules            │
│  • For deep cascades, use restrict at leaf levels + explicit      │
│    deletion order from the application                           │
│  • null/empty reference values always pass validation             │
│  • Target records are checked by id only, not by who can see them │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Schema QA Validation

The `POST /agent/schema/validate` endpoint validates generated schemas against structural
rules and live tenant data. It can validate both single schemas and multi-object application
designs. Returns a quality score (0–100), errors, and warnings.

## Authentication
All endpoints require a Bearer JWT token in the `Authorization` header.
On the `/custom/*` endpoints a tenant public token is not accepted. It gets an empty response.

## Response Pattern
- **Success**: `{ "result": 1, ... }`, HTTP 200.
- **Refused by a check in the handler**: HTTP 200, `{ "result": 2, "error_code": "OBJECT_NOT_FOUND", ... }`.
- **Refused by a raised error**: HTTP 200,
  `{ "result": 2, "error": {"message": "INVALID_REQUEST ACCESS_DENIED"}, "error_code": "INVALID_REQUEST_ACCESS_DENIED" }`.
  The `error_code` is the message in capitals with `_` for spaces.
- **Refused by the collection gate** (`data_access_dict`, or a module collection's `access_dict`):
  HTTP 403 with an empty body. A `collection_id` that is missing or not allowed also gets 403.

## Collection id rules
- Lowercase letters, digits and `_`. 4 to 100 characters. It must not start with `ambivo`.
- These ids name Ambivo's own record types and are refused everywhere: `lead`, `contact`, `account`,
  `opportunity`, `task`, `user`, `order`, `bill`, `product`, `invoice` and `payment`.
- Use exactly the same `collection_id` on every call. It is the key for the object's access rules.
- The backing collection is `amb_<tenant_id>_<collection_id>`. A custom object cannot be renamed.

tags.name: Development Partner Apps
tags.description:
Ambivo staff only. The apps development partners have installed, read live from the
custom object definitions on every call. An app is any value in a custom object's
`hosting_apps`.

tags.name: Custom Objects
tags.description:
Custom object definitions and data records. Each object gets its own
MongoDB collection named `amb_<tenant_id>_<collection_id>` with a JSON Schema validator.

Metadata is stored in `collection_metadata` (custom DB). Access is controlled via
`object_access_dict` (who sees the definition), `data_access_dict` (the letters each
user has on records) and each record's owner and `access_dict`. A `default_access_dict`
is copied to new records. See the overview for both layers.

## Shared Collection Capabilities

Custom Object collections share the same underlying storage as Custom Module collections
(`amb_<tenant_id>_<collection_id>` in `ambivo_customdb`). The following capabilities
work with Custom Object collections by passing the `collection_id` as the identifier:

| Capability | Endpoint | Notes |
|------------|----------|-------|
| Comments | `POST /custom/object/data/comment/manage` | Pass `entity_type` = your `collection_id` |
| Files | `GET/DELETE /custom/object/data/files` | Pass `entity_type` = your `collection_id` in `match_filter_dict` |
| Import | `POST /custom/object/data/import` | Dedicated Custom Objects import endpoint |
| Indexes | `GET /custom/module?action=get-collection-indexes` | Pass `collection_id` |

A custom object cannot be renamed. `rename_one_collection` works only on a collection inside a module.

tags.name: Schema Agents
tags.description:
AI-powered agents for generating and validating custom object schemas.

- **Schema Generator** (`POST /agent/schema/generate`) — generate a single object schema from natural language
- **Application Designer** (`POST /agent/schema/design-app`) — design multi-object applications with relationships
- **Schema QA** (`POST /agent/schema/validate`) — validate generated schemas against structural rules and live tenant data

tags.name: Custom Modules (Legacy)
tags.description:
Legacy module-based custom collections. **The module container concept is planned for
deprecation** — use Custom Objects (`/custom/object`) instead.

Modules group multiple collections under a single container with inherited access control.
Stored in `custom_modules` collection in the main database.

**What is deprecated:** The `/custom/module` CRUD endpoints (creating/updating/deleting
the module container itself — the grouping of collections under a module).

**What is NOT deprecated:** The shared collection capabilities below work with BOTH
Custom Module collections AND Custom Object collections, since both use the same
underlying `amb_<tenant_id>_<collection_id>` collections in the custom database:
- **Comments** (`/custom/module/collection/data/comment/manage`)
- **Files** (`/custom/module/collection/data/files`)
- **Import** (`/custom/module/collection/data/import`)
- **Indexes** (`GET /custom/module?action=get-collection-indexes`)

These endpoints accept any `collection_id` / `entity_type` and resolve it via
`canonical_collection_name()` to the correct backing collection.

**Access on the module routes.** `/custom/module/collection/data` checks the module
collection's `access_dict` as the collection gate. A custom object is in no module,
so on these routes its `data_access_dict` is not checked. The record checks still apply.
Use `/custom/object/data` for custom objects.

**Changing a module** (`PUT` and `DELETE /custom/module`) needs a tenant admin, or `U`
(change) or `D` (delete) in the module's `access_dict`. `delete_collection` drops only
a collection that belongs to the module named by `id`.

get.summary: List every development partner app and the companies it is in (staff only)
get.description:
Only members of Ambivo's own company may call it; anyone else gets
`PARTNER_PROGRAM_STAFF_ONLY`. Computed from `collection_metadata` (custom objects) and
`custom_modules` (with their collections) on every call, so it is exact as apps are
installed and their custom objects deleted. Nothing is stored.

Newest change first. Within an app, partner sandboxes come first. `plan` and `is_pro`
are what the Pro gate sees (Pro, Enterprise, billed outside Ambivo or comped).
A company that no longer exists is listed with `found: false`.

parameters.name: search_text
parameters.description: Part of an app key, a company name or domain, or a partner key. Case does not matter.

parameters.name: match_filter_dict
parameters.description:
JSON with any of `app_key`, `tenant_id`, `is_sandbox` (bool), `is_pro` (bool). An app is
kept when at least one of its companies matches. Any other key: `INVALID_MATCH_FILTER`.

200.description: The page of apps, or a refusal (`result: 2`)

error.message: Only Ambivo staff can see the list of partner apps.

get.summary: List custom objects or get a single object's metadata
get.description:
Without `object_id` / `collection_id`: returns all custom objects visible to
the current user, in `custom_object_list`. A user sees an object when
`object_access_dict` gives them or `*` the letter `R`. Tenant admins see all.
The list also holds records of `type: "standard"`, which every user sees.
The list is not paged.

With `object_id` / `collection_id`: returns a single object's metadata in `custom_object`.
An unknown id returns `{"result": 2, "error_code": "OBJECT_NOT_FOUND"}`.
Returns HTTP 403 with an empty body if the user lacks `R` in `object_access_dict`.

parameters.name: object_id
parameters.description: Object/collection ID to retrieve (omit to list all)

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: One tag. Lists objects that carry it. The value is matched as sent, so a JSON array matches nothing.

parameters.name: hosting_apps
parameters.description: One app key. Lists objects whose `hosting_apps` holds it. The value is matched as sent.

parameters.name: search_text
parameters.description: Part of the object `name`. Case does not matter.

403.description: Access denied — user lacks R permission in object_access_dict

post.description:
Creates both the metadata record in `collection_metadata` and the backing
MongoDB collection `amb_<tenant_id>_<collection_id>` in the custom database
with a `$jsonSchema` validator.

**Tenant admin only.** Anyone else gets `error_code: INVALID_REQUEST_TENANT_ADMIN_REQUIRED`.
Enforces freemium quotas on `custom_structure`. The tenant account must be approved.

The metadata does not keep `schema`. Read the field types back with
`GET /custom/object/data?action=get_schema`.

Errors: `INVALID_REQUEST_INVALID_COLLECTION_ID` (see the collection id rules),
`INVALID_REQUEST_INVALID_COLLECTION_NAME` (a refused name),
`INVALID_REQUEST_CUSTOM_OBJECT_ALREADY_EXISTS`, `INVALID_REQUEST_COLLECTION_ALREADY_EXISTS`,
`INVALID_REQUEST_SCHEMA_MISSING`. A field name with characters other than letters, digits
and `_`, or one that starts with `_id`, is refused with an `INVALID_FIELD_NAME` message.

**Development partner apps need Pro.** A custom object whose `hosting_apps` holds any value
came from a development partner's app. Creating or updating one needs a company on Pro or
Enterprise, billed outside Ambivo (every partner sandbox is), or comped. The 14-day Pro trial
does not count. Otherwise the answer is
`{"result": 2, "error_code": "DEV_PARTNER_APP_REQUIRES_PRO"}` and nothing is written.
A string counts the same as a list. `tags` is never read for this. The same rule applies
to `/custom/module` create and update, and to adding or changing a module's collections.

collection_id.description:
Unique in the tenant. Becomes the suffix of `amb_<tenant_id>_<collection_id>`.
Lowercase letters, digits and `_`, 4 to 100 characters, not starting with `ambivo`.
`lead`, `contact`, `account`, `opportunity`, `task`, `user` and `order` are refused.

schema.description:
Field definitions: `{"<field>": {"bsonType": "<type>", "description": "..."}}`.
Field names: letters, digits and `_`, at most 150 characters, not starting with `_id`.

Types the API converts on write: `string`, `int`, `double`, `bool`, `date`,
`objectId`, `object`, `array`. `timestamp` is stored as `int` (epoch seconds).
Other MongoDB types, such as `long` and `decimal`, are saved as sent.

System fields (`userid`, `updated_by_userid`, `created_ts`, `updated_ts`,
`access_dict`) are always added and replace any field of the same name.
Do not define `file_ids_list`: on a record write it attaches files and is never stored.
`comments` and `attachment_ids_list` are written by the comments endpoint.
Add them to the schema to read them in lists and exports.

The validator runs at the `moderate` level: new records must match, and old
records that do not match are left as they are.

required_fields.description:
Fields a new record must have. MongoDB enforces this on insert. A record without
one fails with a "Document failed validation" error, as `result: 2`.
Optional. Leave it out, or send `[]`, when no field is required.

hosting_apps.description: The app this custom object belongs to. Only development partner apps set it, and any value means the company needs Pro; see "Development partner apps need Pro".

object_access_dict.description: Who can see the definition (`R`). Default: `{creator: CRUD, "*": ["R"]}`. Keys you send are kept; the two defaults are added only when missing.

data_access_dict.description:
The letters each user has on this object's records: `C` create, `R` read, `U` update, `D` delete.
Default: `{creator: CRUD, "*": ["C"]}`. With that default other users can only create.
For a shared app send `{"*": ["C","R","U","D"]}`; each record's owner and `access_dict` still decide which records.

default_access_dict.description: Copied to each new record's `access_dict`. `{"*": ["R"]}` lets everyone in the tenant read new records. If omitted, records get `{}` (owner and tenant admins only).

fields.description: Field names to index. An entry with an empty list drops every index but `_id`.

indexes.description:
MongoDB indexes for query performance. Each entry creates one ascending index on the
backing collection. If one index fails (for example a unique index over duplicate
values), it and the entries after it are skipped, and the call still answers `result: 1`.

formula_fields_list.description:
Computed fields auto-calculated on record create/update via the automation
rules engine. Formulas can reference fields from the same collection or
joined collections. On update, only formulas referencing changed fields
are re-evaluated. Import runs them for each row. `update_many` does not run them.

reference_fields.description:
Cross-collection reference definitions. Keys are field names in the schema,
values define the target collection, field, and on-delete behavior.
References are validated on record create/update. A value that is not a
record id fails validation. A database error lets the write through.
`reference_fields` can point only at other custom objects.

target_field.description: Field in target collection to match against

on_delete.description:
`none` — no action on parent delete (orphans allowed).
`restrict` — block parent delete if children exist.
`nullify` — remove the reference field from the child on parent delete (an empty link is an absent field; `null` is refused).
`cascade` — delete child records on parent delete.

validate.description: Validate referenced record exists on create/update

display_field.description: Field from target to display in UI (optional)

mixed_policies.summary: Object with multiple references and different on_delete policies

project_id.description: FK to projects (restrict — prevent project delete if tasks exist)

assigned_to.description: FK to team_members (nullify — unassign if member removed)

put.description:
**Tenant admin only.** A user who is not an admin gets HTTP 403, or
`INVALID_REQUEST_TENANT_ADMIN_REQUIRED` when `data_access_dict` gives them `U`.
An unknown `collection_id` returns `{"result": 2, "error_code": "OBJECT_NOT_FOUND"}`.

Fields may be sent at the top level or inside a `payload` object.
Updatable fields: `name`, `description`, `icon`, `formula_fields_list`, `reference_fields`,
`tags`, `hosting_apps`, `default_access_dict`, `object_access_dict`, `data_access_dict`,
`schema_meta`/`object_schema`. Each one sent replaces the stored value.
An `object_access_dict` or `data_access_dict` sent without `*` gets `"*": ["R"]` added.

**Development partner apps need Pro**, as for create. The stored `hosting_apps` counts
too, so an update that clears it is refused the same way. Delete is never refused.

**`schema` replaces the whole validator.** Send every field, old and new, with
`required_fields`. Existing records are not changed or checked:
- A field left out of the new `schema` stays in old records. New writes that set it fail with
  `INVALID_KEY_IN_DATA_PAYLOAD`.
- A renamed field is a new field. Old records keep the value under the old name.
  Copy it yourself with `update_many` or record updates.
- A changed type applies to new writes only.

**`indexes`** adds the listed indexes and keeps the others. An empty array drops every
index except `_id`. The stored `indexes` list on the object is not updated.

default_access_dict.description: Replaces the `access_dict` given to new records. Existing records keep theirs.

payload.description: Optional wrapper. When present, the updatable fields are read from it instead of the top level.

schema.description: The complete field list. Replaces the `$jsonSchema` validator on the collection.

required_fields.description: Required fields for the new validator. Read only with `schema`; omitted means none.

indexes.description: Indexes to add. Existing indexes stay. An empty array drops every index except `_id`.

schema_meta.description: UI schema metadata (field labels, display config)

delete.summary: Delete a custom object and drop its backing collection
delete.description:
Deletes `collection_metadata` record **and** drops `amb_<tenant_id>_<collection_id>`.
All data is permanently lost. **Tenant admin only.** A user who is not an admin gets
HTTP 403, or `INVALID_REQUEST_TENANT_ADMIN_REQUIRED` when `data_access_dict` gives them `D`.

An id with no custom object returns `{"result": 2, "error_code": "OBJECT_NOT_FOUND"}` and
drops nothing. Comments and attachments go with the records. Files uploaded onto its records are
deleted too (file record and stored object). A file a contract template uses is kept, and so is
one whose stored object could not be deleted; `files_kept` counts them.
Workflows, automation rules and `reference_fields` in other objects that name it are not removed.

get.summary: Query, export, or aggregate custom object records
get.description:
Collection gate: `R` in `data_access_dict`. Every action returns only the records
the user may read: their own, ones whose `access_dict` grants them `R`, and all for a tenant admin.

**Actions:** `get` (default), `export`, `get_picklist`, `aggregate`, `get_schema`.
Any other action returns `{"result": 2, "error_code": "INVALID_ACTION"}`.

**Records** come back with `id` (the `_id` renamed). Fields of type `date` come back as
`"YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ"` strings.

**Paging:** `page_num` (from 1) and `page_size` (default 30). `total_count` is the number of
records in this page. `gross_count` is the number of records that match, counted on page 1 only;
later pages return `gross_count: 0`. `get_count=true` returns `gross_count` and an empty `data_list`.
With no `sort_dict` the order is the storage order.

**One record:** pass `id`. The record is the only item in `data_list`, or the list is empty.

**`get_picklist`** is `get` with `page_size` 1000 and `page_num` 1.

**`export`** writes the current page to a file. `page_size` applies, so set it high.
Pass `export_settings={"export_to":"json"}` for JSON; CSV is the default.
The response keeps `data_list` and adds `export_url` and `export_msg`. No records means no file.

**`aggregate`** groups the records the user may read. Parameters: `group_by_field` (one field)
or `group_by_fields` (JSON array), optional `aggregate_field`, `match_filter_dict`, `sort_dict`,
and `include_group_docs`: `entity_ids_list` (default), `docs` (whole records) or `none`.
Without a group field the call fails with `INVALID_REQUEST_MISSING_GROUP_BY_FIELD`.
`page_size`, when sent, limits the number of groups.

**`get_schema`** returns the validator's field types in `schema`, system fields included.

parameters.name: match_filter_dict
parameters.description:
JSON MongoDB filter, for example `{"status":"open","qty":{"$gte":5}}`. It is ANDed with the
access rules. A key whose value is empty (`""`, `null`, `[]`, `{}`) is ignored.
Text that is not valid JSON matches no records. To filter on `_id`, use the `id` parameter.
On a `date` field, send ISO 8601 text: `{"work_date":{"$gte":"2026-07-01T00:00:00Z"}}`.
It is read as a date in a plain value, `$eq`, `$ne`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$lt`, `$lte`, `$in` and `$nin`.

parameters.name: search_text
parameters.description: Case-insensitive "contains" match on every string and array field. At most 200 characters. Matched as plain text.

parameters.name: group_by_field
parameters.description: aggregate: one field to group by

403.description: The collection gate refused the user, or the collection_id is missing or not allowed. Empty body.

post.summary: Create a record in a custom object collection
post.description:
Collection gate: `C` in `data_access_dict`.

The API sets `userid` (owner) and `updated_by_userid` to the caller, `created_ts` and
`updated_ts` to now (epoch seconds), and `access_dict` to the object's `default_access_dict`
(or `{}`). Values you send for these fields are replaced.

Every key in `data` must be in the schema, or the call fails with
`INVALID_REQUEST_INVALID_KEY_IN_DATA_PAYLOAD`. Values are converted to the field's type:
- `int` and `double`: numbers, or text such as `"1,200"` and `"-5.50"`. Text that is not a number fails.
- `bool`: `true`/`false`, or the text `"true"`, `"false"`, `"yes"`, `"no"`, `"1"`, `"0"`.
- `date`: ISO text such as `"2026-10-03"`, or epoch seconds. Epoch seconds are read in the server's time zone.
- `string`: any value is turned into text.
- `object` and `array`: a JSON value, or Python-style text of one.
A value that cannot be converted fails with `INVALID_REQUEST_INVALID_<TYPE>_FORMAT`.

`file_ids_list` (optional, in `data`): ids of files already uploaded to this tenant.
They are attached to the new record. It is never stored as a field.

The answer holds the saved record in `data`, as `GET` returns it.
Automation rules, formula fields and workflows (`<collection_id>.create`) run after the save.

with_reference.summary: Child record with foreign key reference

put.summary: Update a single record or bulk-update all records
put.description:
Collection gate: `U` in `data_access_dict`. Any other `action` fails with
`INVALID_REQUEST_INVALID_ACTION`.

**Actions:**

- `update` (default) — Update a single record by `id`. Only the fields in `data` change.
  Values are checked and converted as on create. The user must own the record or have
  `U` in its `access_dict`; otherwise the answer is
  `{"result": 2, "error_code": "RECORD_NOT_FOUND_OR_ACCESS_DENIED"}`.
  A save that changes nothing answers `result: 1, modified_count: 0`.
  When something changed, `updated_ts` and `updated_by_userid` are set, and automation rules,
  formula fields and workflows (`<collection_id>.update`) run.
  `data.file_ids_list` attaches uploaded files, as on create.
- `update_many` — Apply `$set` to many records. A tenant admin sets **ALL** records.
  Anyone else sets the records they own or have `U` on. `data` is not checked against
  the schema, so this can add a field that is not in it. No rules, formulas or workflows run.
  **Use with caution** — there is no undo. Empty `data` fails with `INVALID_REQUEST_MISSING_DATA`.

`data` may set `userid` (the owner) and `access_dict`. Use `access_dict` to share a record.

### Examples

**Update a single record:**
```json
{
  "collection_id": "support_tickets",
  "action": "update",
  "id": "65a1b2c3d4e5f60001234567",
  "data": {"status": "closed"}
}
```

**Add a new column to all records:**
```json
{
  "collection_id": "support_tickets",
  "action": "update_many",
  "data": {"priority_label": "normal"}
}
```

**Update an existing column across all records (e.g. reset access_dict):**
```json
{
  "collection_id": "support_tickets",
  "action": "update_many",
  "data": {"access_dict": {"*": ["R", "U"]}}
}
```

action.description:
`update` — single record (requires `id`).
`update_many` — bulk-set field(s) on every record you may update (all records for a tenant admin).

suppress_automation_triggers.description: `true` skips the workflow event. Used by workflows that write records.

add_column.summary: Add new column to all records

update_all_rows.summary: Update existing column across all records

update_reference.summary: Re-assign child to different parent (reference validated)

single.summary: Single record updated (data is the whole record)

denied.summary: The user may not update this record, or it does not exist

delete.description:
Collection gate: `D` in `data_access_dict`. Parameters go in the query string. Permanent removal.

- `delete` (default): one record by `id`. A record the user does not own and has no `D` on
  returns `{"result": 2, "error_code": "ACCESS_DENIED"}`. A missing record returns
  `{"result": 2, "deleted_count": 0}`.
- `delete_many`: `ids_list` as a JSON array. Deletes the listed records the user may delete.
  The others are named in `not_deleted_ids`. If none may be deleted the answer is `ACCESS_DENIED`.
- `delete_all`: a tenant admin empties the collection. Anyone else deletes every record they may
  delete. It skips workflows and automation rules. An empty result answers `result: 2`.

All three apply `reference_fields` policies of child objects: `restrict` blocks the delete first,
then `nullify` and `cascade` run. `delete` and `delete_many` also run workflows
(`<collection_id>.delete`) and automation rules. `suppress_automation_triggers=true` skips the
workflow event.

Files uploaded onto the deleted records are deleted with them, and so are the files of children a
`cascade` deletes. `files_deleted` and `files_kept` count them. A file a contract template uses,
or one whose stored object could not be deleted, is kept.

partly.summary: delete_many where some records belong to other people

denied.summary: The user may not delete this record

error.message: Cannot delete: 3 record(s) in 'order_items' reference this record via 'order_id'. Delete or unlink the child records first.

multi_level_cascade.summary: Delete order: its order_items are deleted; their item_notes stay

post.summary: Add, get, update, or delete comments and attachments on a custom object record
post.description:
Synonym route for `/custom/module/collection/data/comment/manage`.
Pass your Custom Object `collection_id` as `entity_type`.

The user must be able to read the record (owner, `R` in its `access_dict`, or tenant admin).
Adding or deleting attachments needs `U` on the record. Otherwise the answer is
`{"result": 2, "error_code": "RECORD_NOT_FOUND_OR_ACCESS_DENIED"}`.

Comments are stored in the record's `comments` array, newest last. `idx` is the 0-based
position in that array. Only the author can update or delete a comment, and system comments
cannot be changed. A change that does nothing answers `result: 2` with `msg` ending in
`NO_ACTION_PERFORMED`.

`attachment_ids_list` holds message attachment ids. `add` stores them on the record and adds
an "Attachment added" comment. `delete` removes them and deletes the stored attachment.

get.summary: List files attached to custom object records
get.description:
Synonym route for `/custom/module/collection/data/files`.
Pass your Custom Object `collection_id` as `entity_type` in `match_filter_dict`.

Lists files attached to one record. Whoever may read the record (`R` on the object and on the
record) sees every file on it, whoever uploaded it; `POST /user/file/manage` `get_url` opens
them on the same terms. Someone who may not read the record sees only the files they uploaded.
On a custom module collection, a user who is not a tenant admin sees only their own files.

A file is attached by uploading it to `POST /user/file_upload` with
`storefile_custom_fields={"entity_type":"<collection_id>","entity_id":"<record id>","is_custom_module_entity":true}`,
or by sending its id in `data.file_ids_list` when you create or update the record.

parameters.name: match_filter_dict
parameters.description: JSON with `entity_type` (the collection_id) and `entity_id` (the record id). Both are required.

delete.summary: Delete a file attached to a custom object record
delete.description:
Synonym route for `DELETE /custom/module/collection/data/files`.
Deletes the stored file, scoped to the caller and the tenant.

post.summary: Bulk import records into a custom object collection
post.description:
Async import — validates and transforms records via `dict_to_collection_data_payload()`,
then launches a Celery background job. Returns a job ID for status tracking.

Collection gate: `C` in `data_access_dict`.

Each row is checked loosely here: keys not in the schema are dropped, and values that
cannot be converted are dropped. The job then creates each row as `POST /custom/object/data`
does: the importer owns it, `default_access_dict` applies, references are checked, and
rules, formulas and workflows run per row.

Transformation errors are collected (up to 10 returned in response).
A row left with no schema fields is skipped without an error.
If no valid records can be extracted, the import is rejected.
Follow the job with `GET /user/data_import/manage?id=<import_id>`.

field_mappings_dict.description: Schema field to source column, e.g. `{"title": "Title", "status": "Status"}`. Columns whose names already match need no entry.

import_name.description: Display name for the import job

value.message: Import job scheduled for background processing

error.message: No valid records could be extracted from the import data

get.summary: List custom modules or get collection indexes
get.description:
Without `action`: lists modules in `custom_module_list`. A tenant admin sees all. Anyone else
sees a module when its `access_dict` or one of its collections' `access_dict` names them or `*`.
Paged with `page_num` and `page_size` (default 30); `id` returns one module.
Ids come back as `id`.

With `action=get-collection-indexes`: the indexes on the collection named by `collection_id`.
Works for custom objects too.

post.description:
Creates a module container. Collections added separately via
`PUT /custom/module` with `action=add_one_collection`. Any signed-in user of an approved
tenant can create one. Its `access_dict` gets the creator `C,R,U,D` and `*` `R` when missing.
`collections` in the body is ignored.

put.summary: Update module, add/update/rename collections, manage indexes
put.description:
**Actions:** `update_module`, `add_one_collection`, `update_one_collection`,
`rename_one_collection`, `collection_add_one_index`, `collection_drop_indexes`,
`collection_drop_all_indexes`

Needs a tenant admin, or `U` in the module's `access_dict`. Otherwise the call fails with
`INVALID_REQUEST_ACCESS_DENIED` (or `INVALID_REQUEST_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`).

- `update_module`: sets the fields sent. The answer has `update_module_response` and no
  top-level `result`; `update_module_response.result` is 1 only when something changed.
- `add_one_collection`: `collection` needs `id`, `schema` and `required_fields`. Without
  `access_dict` the collection gets `{<caller>: [C,R,U,D]}`. The id follows the collection id rules.
- `update_one_collection`: replaces the collection entry. `schema` and `required_fields` are required.
- `rename_one_collection`: renames a collection inside this module. Custom objects cannot be renamed.
- Index actions take `collection_id`; `collection_add_one_index` takes `index_dict`
  (`{"fields": [...], "unique": false}`); `collection_drop_indexes` takes `indexes: [{"name": ...}]`.

delete.description:
Without `action`: deletes entire module + all collections.
With `action=delete_collection`: deletes one collection. Cascades to automation rules.
Either way, files uploaded onto the dropped collections' records are deleted too, and each entry
of `collection_delete_response` counts them (`files_deleted`, `files_kept`).

Needs a tenant admin, or `D` in the module's `access_dict`. For a user who is not an admin,
`collection_id` must be a collection of the module named by `id`
(`INVALID_REQUEST_COLLECTION_NOT_IN_MODULE` otherwise).

get.summary: Query, export, aggregate, or get schema/chart config of collection data
get.description:
**Actions:** `get` (default), `export`, `picklist`/`get_picklist`, `get_entity_ids`,
`aggregate`, `chart_config`, `get_schema`

Collection gate: `R` in the module collection's `access_dict`. A custom object has no module,
so here it gets no collection gate. Every action returns only the records the user may read,
as on `GET /custom/object/data`. Paging, filters, `id`, records and `aggregate` work the same way.

- `export` returns `export_url` and `export_msg` without `data_list`. `airtable` sends the page to Airtable.
- `get_entity_ids`: `entity_ids` as a JSON array. Returns the readable ones among them.
  `export_to=csv|json` (or `export_settings`) writes them to a file.
- `chart_config`: field names from the schema. Text and boolean fields are `groupable_fields`;
  number fields are `aggregate_fields`.
- An unknown action returns `{"result": 2, "error": "invalid_action"}`.

parameters.name: tenant_scope
parameters.description: Accepted and has no effect. The record checks always apply; a tenant admin sees all records anyway.

post.summary: Create a record or retrieve records by ID
post.description:
**Actions:** `add` (default), `get_entity_ids`.
Collection gate: `C` in the module collection's `access_dict`, for both actions.
`add` works as `POST /custom/object/data`. `get_entity_ids` returns only readable records.

200.description: Record created, or records by id

put.description:
Collection gate: `U` in the module collection's `access_dict`. Works as
`PUT /custom/object/data`: `action` is `update` (default) or `update_many`, and the record checks apply.

delete.description:
Collection gate: `D` in the module collection's `access_dict`. Works as
`DELETE /custom/object/data`, including `delete_all` and the record checks.

post.summary: Add, get, update, or delete comments and attachments on a record
post.description:
**Shared endpoint** — works with both Custom Module and Custom Object collections.
Pass your Custom Object `collection_id` as `entity_type`.
Same rules and answers as `POST /custom/object/data/comment/manage`.

get.summary: List files attached to collection records
get.description:
**Shared endpoint** — works with both Custom Module and Custom Object collections.
Pass your Custom Object `collection_id` as `entity_type` in `match_filter_dict`.
Same rules and answers as `GET /custom/object/data/files`.

parameters.name: match_filter_dict
parameters.description: JSON with `entity_type` (the collection_id) and `entity_id` (the record id). Both are required.

delete.summary: Delete a file attached to a collection record
delete.description: Deletes the stored file, scoped to the caller and the tenant.

post.summary: Bulk import records into a module collection
post.description:
Async import — validates/transforms records, launches Celery background job.
Returns job ID for status tracking. Transformation errors collected (up to 10).
Collection gate: `C` in the module collection's `access_dict` (none for a custom object).
Rows are handled as on `POST /custom/object/data/import`.

value.message: Import job scheduled for background processing

error.message: No valid records could be extracted

post.summary: Generate a custom object schema from natural language
post.description:
AI-powered schema generation. Supports iterative conversation via `session_id`.
Returns `status: "more-info-needed"` with clarifying questions or `status: "complete"`
with the generated `schema_meta`.

Includes automatic QA validation (`qa_report`) in the response.

The tenant's existing custom objects are read by the server and offered as reference
targets. `existing_custom_objects` in the body is ignored.

`full_metadata` holds the object definition without `schema`. Before `POST /custom/object`,
build `schema` from `schema_meta.attributes` (one `bsonType` per attribute) and review the
access dicts: `object_access_dict` gives the caller only `R`, and `data_access_dict` names only the caller.

description.description: Natural language description of the object

existing_custom_objects.description: Ignored. The server reads the tenant's objects itself.

existing_schema.description: A schema_meta to edit instead of starting from nothing. JSON text is accepted.

context.description: Optional extra context for the generator

I need an order items tracker that references my orders collection

post.summary: Design a multi-object application with cross-collection relationships
post.description:
AI-powered application designer that produces multiple custom object schemas
with `reference_fields`, indexes, relationships, and `creation_order`.

Use this to design entire applications (e.g., "Property management app with
buildings, units, tenants, and maintenance requests").

Includes automatic QA validation (`qa_report`) in the response.

When QA finds problems it cannot fix, the answer has `status: "qa-fixing"` and questions.
Call again with the same `session_id` and the answer in `description`.
Each object also carries `collection_id` and `full_metadata` (without `schema`, as in generate).

description.description: Natural language description of the application

existing_custom_objects.description: Existing objects that new objects can reference

session_id.description: Continue a design after QA questions

post.summary: Validate a generated schema or application design
post.description:
QA validation endpoint. Validates schemas against:
- Structural rules (required fields, valid types, key format)
- Semantic rules (select options, reference targets, primary field)
- Cross-object consistency (for application designs)
- Live tenant data (detects key collisions, novel types)

Returns a quality score (0–100), errors, and warnings.

schema_meta.description: The schema_meta dict to validate (required for mode=schema)

reference_fields.description: Optional reference_fields to validate alongside schema

app_result.description: The full app_result from /agent/schema/design-app (required for mode=application)

fetch_live_samples.description: If true, compare against live tenant data in customdb

post.description:
Pass a current `schema_meta` and a natural language refinement request.
Returns the updated schema with changes applied.

post.summary: Suggest additional attributes for an object type
post.description: Given an object type and optionally existing attributes, suggests useful additional fields.

object_type.description: Type of object (e.g. task, project, property)
